items.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024
items.q: And I have tried, I tried to record that tune and it’s not anything the way J.J. does it.

ctx.x: There’s a term you used a couple of times, you were talking about the first time you heard J.J. Johnson and then in a live situation with Ed Pratt’s band. And you were listening to these players and you said, “I was wrecked.” And I was thinking, well some people the reaction they would have had would be to give up. To say no way, no way am I ever going to do that so I’ll find something else to do. But you chose not to give up.

And I didn’t give up and I haven’t given up yet. J.J., I heard J.J. play a tune, one of his tunes, called “Overdrive.” I still can’t play it. But the way he played it so fluently and so fluidly. He was — the way he approached those changes — I still cannot do it the way he did it. And I have tried, I tried to record that tune and it’s not anything the way J.J. does it. You know so, and I can’t say if he got it naturally or maybe he learned how to play

like that. You know? But I think he had the natural ability. Because the way J.J. plays the trombone and the way I play the trombone is very similar. Like we don’t play with the double tongue, the double tongue, like most trombone players can do, you know, real good. I can’t do that either. You know, but he had a fast tongue and a fast single tongue, and a fast slide. You know? I just found out last week that a lot of tunes that — a lot of positions I play in first position they can play in fourth position. And I…
